claim: The new early `return null` when `suppressSourceGeneration is true` runs right after the attribute arguments are read. That is before any member, key or accessibility analysis, so for an opted-out type the collector never reaches the code that reports MsgPack004/005/015/003/012. The fix hides all analyzer diagnostics for `SuppressSourceGeneration = true` types instead of restoring them. This is the opposite of the requirement ('the MessagePack analyzer still reports its diagnostics (MsgPack0xx rules)') and of the 3.1.0 behaviour. Ledger L14 only exempts the generation-only rules MsgPack011/016/017, not 003/004/005/012/015.

claim: The new early `return null` when `suppressSourceGeneration is true` skips the whole TypeCollector analysis for the type. A `[MessagePackObject(SuppressSourceGeneration = true)]` class with a public property that has no [Key] or [IgnoreMember] therefore gets no MsgPack004. MsgPack003/005 for its member types are also dropped, because the members are never visited. This is the opposite of the acceptance criterion that the analyzer still reports MsgPack0xx diagnostics with SuppressSourceGeneration = true. L14 only exempts the generation-only rules (011, 016, 017), not 003/004/005.

claim: The early return for SuppressSourceGeneration=true happens before the contractAttr-null/MsgPack003 and member-level checks, so users who set SuppressSourceGeneration=true will no longer see analyzer diagnostics for those types (MsgPack004 missing Key/IgnoreMember, MsgPack005 mixed keys, duplicate keys, MsgPack007, etc.). The requirement says analyzer diagnostics must still be reported when suppressed, and 3.1.0 reported them. L14 only exempts generation-only diagnostics (MsgPack011/016/017), not these. The change therefore leaves the reported bug unfixed for the majority of rules and may make it worse.

claim: The `continue` added after DoNotMixStringAndIntKeys changes the collected member set for types that mix key kinds. Previously the member was still processed and added; now it is dropped. For types where the diagnostic is only a warning/ignored, or when the generator still emits code, the generated formatter's members, and so the generated output users snapshot or compile, change without opt-in. Behaviour for unset SuppressSourceGeneration is supposed to stay unchanged.

claim: The new `ContainsKey` guards silently discard the second member when two members share the same int or string key. Before, `Add` threw, so the generator or analyzer failure was visible. Now the generated formatter is produced without that member, and no diagnostic in this hunk flags the duplicate, so the member's data is never serialized. The dynamic resolver throws on duplicate keys at run time. The early return above means these guards only run for generated (non-suppressed) types, so this does not help the reported bug and adds a silent-drop path.
